about: FoodBlock 1.7: every closed list and grammar in the spec (core.md, modules/ and profiles/), for code to load. Where the spec states a list, it matches this file exactly. Year zero is 1.6: no older shape is read, and 1.7 adds to it except the few deletions CHANGELOG.md lists.
types_about: Three moods, no fourth. `is` is a reading: it binds its signer's name to its truth, obliges no one to act, and any key may sign one, a machine's included. `must` is a promise: it binds its signer's property to its condition, and only a person signs one; a `transfer` is a promise whose condition is already met. `may` is a grant: the signer's consent to another acting for him within limits, only a person signs one, and a holder passes on only a narrower part. `actor` and `thing` are readings (that this key, that thing, is so); a `transform` with no inputs (a first use) is a reading, evidence a judge reads and never title made by a signature. An answer that accepts is a promise, written with the type of the block it answers. A decline is a reading: an `observe` with `refs.answers` and `state.status` `declined`; one written before the three moods with the answered block's type is read the same (promises.md, Answers).
type_about: Any other type name matching grammar.type_name is open: stored and passed on, no authority.

needs.about: The blocks a block names for its meaning: `read` reads them (core.md, section 8), and a block that names one not held, not valid or not read is not read. A block's pieces (its author's genesis, the block its `refs.key` names, and that one's pieces) are `valid`'s and are not listed here. No block waits for its `prev`.

refs.about: Shared ref keys are these lists plus the verbs and the causal keys. refs.of names the kind an instance belongs to; state.kind is a label. refs.key names the key grant that brought in the key that signed the block (identity.md, refs.key).

refs_single_about: These links hold exactly one id; an array there is `grammar` (core.md, section 1): an answer answers one block, a stop or a new version updates one, a block speaks as one circle, acts under one grant, and a grant passes on one parent. A promise's sides (from, to) are one id each too (promises.md, Sides: `shape`).
statuses_about: `resumed` is the author's own `updates` of their pause (a stop naming occurrences), never an answer. `lifted` is a block's `updates` of a machine lock (`machine_lock`), never an answer and never of any other block. A counter-offer is an answer (a promise with refs.answers) whose state carries new terms and no status; it is the one answer without a status.

machine_lock.about: A machine lock (authority.md, A machine lock): a grant of kind `stop` that carries `how`, aimed at the machine by `refs.subject`. `how` is hand (placed with a hand on the machine) or far (placed from away); `reach` is the signer's own name for what the lock covers; `placer` the id of the person who placed it; `safe` the name of the safe state chosen. A lift is an `updates` of the lock with status `lifted`; `state.checked: true` with `refs.confirms` the owner's stake is the owner's lift. A grant of kind stop without `how` is read as before.

stop.occurrences: { occurrences: [start times, or the hashes of the blocks that started them] }: named occurrences of a standing promise

circle.removal_rule: Each circle states its removal rule at founding, state.removal { needed: N } on the circle actor; with none stated, no one who holds admit or remove is removed (folds.md, Counts). needed 1: any holder of remove alone removes anyone, as in a chat group's admins. Removing a holder of admit or remove takes at least `needed` different holders of remove, the remover among them, each stopping that same member grant. The member removed never counts among them.
circle.roles_shape: state.roles: [{ name, powers }]; the founding block is the founder's first member grant, giving the first role; powers are from `powers` and from profile powers, and no one gives a power they do not hold
circle.change_rule: state.change: [{ rule, needed }] on the founding block of a circle: `rule` the name of a key of the circle actor's state, `needed` a count of the members by Counts (folds.md): a whole number, `all`, or { of_members: "p/q" }. A version of the circle that changes that rule moves every member once that many members are on it (circles.md, Versions). A rule named twice, or a founding block with no such line for it, moves only those who sign the version. Read only from the founding block. Every other fold of the circle reads the rules as they now stand: each rule a carried version moves takes that version's value (circles.md, Versions).
circle.needed_rule: state.needed: { sign: N } on the circle actor: a block signed as the circle speaks for it once N different holders of sign have signed it, its author and holders who `confirms` it, each in their own block's fold and within the cuts of their ended grants. With none, one holder's signature, as for any block. Admitting and removing keep their own rules (removal).

genesis.private_about: A genesis may carry any audience (decision H10): public, or a sorted list of commitments with state.nonce, as any private block. A reader verifies it once it holds it; a node waits on a block whose author's genesis it lacks, as for any need. A genesis has no public header: a reader outside its audience is sent nothing of it.
genesis.recognised: An actor is judged as a genesis when it has state.public_key_sign or has no refs.author; it is then held to this list alone (bad_genesis), and its signature must open with its own public_key_sign (bad_genesis, never bad_signature).
genesis.optional_about: Besides `required`, a genesis may carry suite, public_key_encrypt, reach and keepers (key_fields, all but roles, voices and shown_key), keepers being required with reach, and, when its audience is a list, its nonce (private); never roles, name or marks (bad_genesis).

required.about: What a block needs beyond the common five (core.md, section 7), by its role: a block that starts something needs the fields of its type; a block that replies to another needs refs.answers (or, for the author's own stop, refs.updates) and state.status.

transfer: one of refs.to_owner, refs.to_holder, refs.to_place, state.count

replies.unless: the reply is a counter-offer: a promise with refs.answers whose state carries new terms and no status (promises.md, Answers)

fields.about: The base fields of the closed types. Every closed type may also carry `every`. A closed block says more only through a schema it names (core.md, section 7). The open types (thing, observe, transform and any new word) list nothing here: their fields are described by the base schemas (spec/schemas), and nothing is refused for them.

key_fields.about: Defined once. A genesis carries public_key_sign, public_key_encrypt, suite, reach and keepers; a key grant carries public_key_sign, public_key_encrypt, suite, voices, keepers and shown_key; a member grant and a circle's actor carry roles (identity.md).

shapes.amount_about: An amount (encoding.md, Shapes): value a decimal, unit the author's text, of (optional) an id: the kind. Two amounts are of one kind when unit is the same text and of the same id, or neither has one. Beside refs.what, and as a thing's pack, an amount carries no of (shape). Money is an amount; there is no other shape for it.
shapes.price_figure_about: A price fixed later (promises.md, Terms): `figure` the kind of `observe` whose `state.amount` is the figure, `by` the readers (ids or circle#role), `signers` how many different ones must have signed the same figure, `deadline` and `keepers` the window on a named clock, and optionally `fraction` (a decimal from 0 to 1: the share of the figure the price is), `min` and `max` (amounts of the figure's kind: a figure outside them does not count). It is a bare price's shape, never a line's.
shapes.input_about: an item of a make's state.inputs: from one of its refs.derives_from, amount in that input's kind (things.md, A make)

where.values: decimal strings; radius is an amount in m

shapes.when_window_about: Any of these, at least one, alone or beside the keys of a range or a relative form; not_before and not_after are times, takes a duration (blocks.md, profiles/tasks.md).
shapes.when_event_about: A `when` that follows an event is { after, wait } with `after` an observe kind (any text that is not an id): due `wait` after the receiving side's observe of that kind `for` the promise, dated by the named clock (promises.md, Relative time). `after` an id is the relative form of a block.
shapes.keepers_about: A named clock (blocks.md, A named clock): `names` a non-empty sorted list of block ids, each naming a line (that block's key's blocks after it; a person's id names her genesis key's line); `needed` by Counts (folds.md): a set of one needs none, a larger set states it. It sits in the word whose time or order it reads: a condition `within` or `without`, a promise's terms, a transfer, a grant, a list of voices.

voice.about: One voice of a list, exactly one of these key sets (identity.md, Her voices): key a signing key in its suite's grammar; key_hash a hash; names a non-empty sorted list of ids with needed by Counts (folds.md). wait and reach are durations. A list is an array of voices, the first a key or key_hash, each key, key_hash and id once in all; it is empty in one place only, a key grant that leaves no voice and so ends her identity.

places.about: A shape is read only at a place the protocol gives it, never by a field name deeper in. The places are the fields of a block's state, of its terms and scope, and of each item of its lines, split and inputs. A value at a place is read by its own keys, and the fields that `field_shape` gives the shape `shape` hold an object, never a bare value. A map nested under a field is data: nothing in it is read as a shape. The fields named in data are not places: what they hold is data (a schema's fields, grounds and roles name things), so nothing in them is read as a shape.

field_shape_about: Which shape a field name holds, where the protocol gives it a place (shapes.places): time (grammar.time; `when` also takes the forms of shapes.when), date (grammar.date), duration (grammar.duration), shape (exactly one of the keyed shapes in `shapes`, never a bare value). The lists a check asks for (every time field, every duration field) are read from this table.

kind_fields.about: The typed fields of a kind (core.md, section 3), one rule for every kind. Under a type and a kind (`state.kind`), each line is `field:shape`: the field a path in the state (`terms.reveal_by` is state.terms.reveal_by) and the shape `text`, `hash` (a SHA-256 digest in hex), `id` (grammar.id), `time` (grammar.time), `count` (a whole number of at least 1) or `in:<list>` (one of a closed list named here by its path). A shape ending in `!` is asked for: the field must be there (`shape` otherwise). A field that is there must have its shape (`shape`, or `grammar` for a hash or an id, `time` for a time); a field left out is asked for by nothing here unless its shape ends in `!`, and a field not listed is not read. Every line restates what the module that owns the kind already says in words (authority.md, A witness; consent.md, section 2; profiles/pools.md, the schema draw). receipt: refs.derives_from the blocks it names, one or more, no state field asked for. dropped: refs.derives_from the blocks or receipts a node no longer holds, on the log that took them in (nodes.md, The arrival log). received: refs.for the deal, state.amount what came, state.line where the deal has lines: the receiver's own word against herself (folds.md, What is left, The other side).

grammar.id_about: A bare id is SHA-256. Any other hash carries its name and a colon (suites, hashes).

grammar_notes.about: Every pattern is an ECMAScript regular expression, anchored at both ends: `$` means the end of the text, never before a final newline. A reader in another engine anchors the end exactly (Python: re.fullmatch, or \Z), or a value with a trailing newline would pass.
grammar_notes.duration: Written without lookahead so every regex engine runs it.
grammar_notes.time: The pattern is the shape; the value must also be a real calendar instant (no 30 February).
grammar_notes.hour: A time of day with its own offset from UTC, as hours of a machine's fence are written (authority.md, A machine's fence): HH:MM then Z or +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The offset is part of the word, so no time zone database is read; a place that changes its clock re-signs.
grammar_notes.zone: Shaped like an IANA time zone name: a name with no slash (UTC, and the legacy names GMT, CET, EST5EDT, Zulu), or Area/Location with one or two slashes (Europe/London, America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires). The protocol checks the shape, never a list of zones.
grammar_notes.rrule_part: One part of an RRULE value (RFC 5545), KEY=VALUE; the parts are joined by ; and exactly one is FREQ, from repeat.freq.
grammar_notes.date: The pattern is the shape; the value must also be a real calendar date.

hashes_about: A hash name a reader knows is the bare SHA-256 and every `prefix` of a hash that a suite in `suites` (not `future`) uses: sm3. sha3-256 is listed for the future suite and is unknown until that suite is fixed in vectors.

suites.about: A suite names a hash, a signature algorithm and an envelope together. A key names its suite in state.suite; left out, std. A block is hashed with the hash of the suite of the key that signed it. A reader refuses an unknown suite (refusals.codes.block.unknown_suite).

passkey.form: r then s (64 bytes), the length of authenticatorData (2 bytes, big-endian), authenticatorData, clientDataJSON
passkey.challenge: base64url, no padding, of SHA-256 of the signed bytes (for a block, its id)

sm.key_about: SM4 takes 16 bytes: the content key is the first 16 of its 32 random bytes and HKDF derives 16 bytes (privacy.md, Envelope).

pq.status: noted, not usable until sizes are fixed in vectors; a signature must still fit limits.signature_bytes

messages.public_block_about: A message is canonical JSON, whole, and exactly { block, signature }: any other key refuses it (shape). No suite and no version travel beside a block.
messages.proof_about: A signed request carries exactly one of counter (an integer above the highest the node has seen from the signer) or challenge (issued by the node, used once). It carries no time.
messages.pull_answer_about: log is given only when the request names one (nodes.md, Pull); a block with no receipt on that log has no arrival number on it and is not served under it.
messages.push_answer_order: taken and refused: ascending by hash, a block's codes in the order of refusals.codes.block. unjudged and unread: ascending by hash, each needs ascending, each codes in list order. equivocations: each pair sorted, the list sorted. held: ascending by hash.
messages.signature_about: A key signs four shapes, each canonical JSON: a block's header (header, header_optional), a genesis's own bytes, a request without its signature key, an answer without its signature key. A header has hash; a genesis has type; a request has signer and node; an answer has node and neither signer nor hash. A pull answer's request is the bare SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON of the whole signed request. header_signature is the block's one signature. An envelope plaintext is the canonical JSON of the plaintext object.
messages.admission_about: per_stranger and strangers_per_day count asks: blocks that name one of the node's people in a ref, never a block's pieces

peers.about: Three peers: micro, edge, node. A micro that acts and an index are variants.
peers.micro_clockless: a micro may leave out at and when on observe, transform and transfer; its edge writes an observe of kind receipt

optional_profiles.about: Optional. A node that has never heard of a profile still accepts every block in it.

successor.close_rule: A close counts when its author is the successor grant's refs.to and not the person; the grant stands in the close's causal past, covers the close where it states scope.types, and no stop of it nor the successor's decline or leaving is in that past; no counted close of its author is in its causal past; and the witnesses' key grant (identity.md) stands in its causal past, by a voice that does not name the successor. It ends authority, never a promise, for blocks that have it in their causal past, bar what state.continues names.

counted_in.input: a ballot result, a commitment, the named counter
counted_in.output: true when the result is signed by that counter and lists the commitment in counted

output.epoch: the current epoch; 0 is the circle actor's key
output.keys: the encryption keys of the epoch's counted rekeys, sorted

residency.regions: plain labels the node's promise and the author's request name, compared by exact equality; the protocol gives none a meaning

refusals.about: Every refusal is { hash, code, detail }. block: why `valid` refuses a block's bytes, final for those bytes, bar `unmet` and `unknown_suite`, which wait. read: why `read` cannot read a valid block; never a refusal: the block is kept, not read. fold: why a fold counts a block for nothing, or gives no answer. message: why a node refuses a message. `valid` runs the checks in `checks` (core.md, section 8, checks 1 to 6) in order and stops at the first that finds anything. `read` runs check 7 and gives every code it finds, in the order of `read`, which lists every code it can give.

block.not_canonical: bytes that are not exactly the canonical bytes of a value that follows strict writing: any spelling but the one, a null, a number that is not a whole number in range, text that is not well-formed, a set out of order or with a repeat, or not exactly type, state and refs
block.float: a number with a fraction or exponent in a value that never was text (CBOR, or a value handed to a writer)
block.integer_range: a whole number outside integers.min..integers.max, or -0, in a value that never was text
block.decimal: a decimal string outside grammar.decimal, or with more digits than limits.decimal_digits
block.grammar: an id, salt, nonce, role ref, language tag, type name, RRULE or time zone outside its grammar
block.time: a time, date or duration outside its grammar
block.calendar: a time or date in the right shape that is not a real calendar instant
block.shape: an amount, price, range, mark, input, split, when, where or reveal without its keys; an amount with of beside refs.what or as a thing's pack; a transfer with state.amount and to_holder or to_place; a refrain flag, a needed or removal rule, a role list item or an event repeat not in its shape
block.type_name: a type that does not match grammar.type_name
block.size_limit: its bytes are over limits.block_bytes (a sealed copy's block, once opened), or open more than limits.depth levels
block.after_limit: refs.after names more than limits.after_heads heads
block.audience: an audience that is neither public nor a sorted list of commitments
block.bad_genesis: a genesis with author, prev, after or seq, missing a genesis field, with reach and no keepers, or not signed by its own key
block.chain: a block that is not a genesis lacks refs.author, refs.prev or state.seq
block.at_missing: no at on a block that is not an observe, transform or transfer
block.unmet: a piece is not held, or held only as its header (its author's genesis, the block its refs.key names, and that block's pieces): not a refusal but a wait; fetching it cures it
block.bad_piece: a piece it rests on is held and refused (its id is the hash of its bytes, so it can never become valid): final, naming the piece and its code
block.bad_hash: an id sent with it is not the hash of its canonical bytes in the suite of the key that signed it (no label names the suite)
block.bad_signature: the key its pieces name does not open its signature over its header (a genesis: over its own bytes), or the block its refs.key names is not a key grant of its author about its author
block.unknown_suite: a key that names a suite the reader does not know, or a key, signature or id outside its suite's grammar, or a piece that waits on such a suite; not a refusal but a wait: judged again when the reader knows the suite
block.names_missing: read's own code: a block it names for its meaning (needs) is not held; listed with the id of each such block. The cure is to fetch it. The block is kept, not read
block.names_unread: read's own code: a block it names for its meaning (needs) is held and not valid or not read; listed with the id of each such block. Fetching does not cure it. The block is kept, not read
block.required: a closed block missing a required field (core.md, section 7): a refrain without until, a to_role without refs.to, a rekey without refs.as; a transfer that names no instance and no to_owner
block.undeclared_ref: on a closed type, a ref key neither shared nor declared by its schema
block.undeclared_field: on a closed type, a state field neither its type's base field nor declared by its schema
block.status_not_answer: a status on a block that neither answers nor updates its author's own
block.bad_status: a status not in statuses, stopped without a valid stop, or a stop beside any other status or none
block.deal_not_named: an answer or counter in a deal that does not name the deal's first promise, exactly, in refs.for
block.lines: a line without an id unique in the promise, a top-level price or quantity beside lines, or refs.what not the lines' what
block.wider_than_parent: a child grant's scope or depth wider than its parent's on any field
block.not_receiver: a grant passed on by someone other than its parent's receiver, or, for a parent made to a circle, by a block not signed as that circle
block.bad_roles: a circle roles list whose powers are not in powers (or a profile's powers) or repeat one, a role name that is empty, repeated or holds #, or a founder with no first role

fold.not_a_side: signed by neither side nor an agent under a side's live grant
fold.open_offer_counter: a counter to an open offer, by the taker or the offerer in a chain of counters: it ends nothing (only the author ends an open offer) and binds nothing until the side that did not sign it answers it accepted; that accept of a counter of the chain is an allocation, a one-to-one deal on the counter's own terms whose quantity counts against the open offer's
fold.not_live: acts under a grant that is not live, or outside its scope (its types by exact name, its parties), or is a block that moves things or binds someone with no trusted schema saying undo ok and neither a specific accepted ask nor a grant naming it with a limit (a commitment to one, or a visible one)
fold.not_member: a new version of a circle, or an acceptance of one, by someone who is no member in the circle's fold of the block's causal past, or a version that updates a block that is neither the circle nor a counted version: it counts for nothing
fold.no_role: signs as a circle without a role with the sign power, in the circle's fold of its causal past
fold.not_counted: a settling block the receiver has not accepted and no confirmer the grounds name has confirmed
fold.pair: one of a pair that name one prev or state one seq, or a later block of that key (a draw of a fork takes nothing: folds.md, What is left): proof, counted for nothing of what is owed to its signer
fold.quote_only: an accept of a quote request: an agent's ask whose grant does not cover its type binds no one
fold.waiting: a word that does not yet stand (blocks.md, Finality); listed in `waiting` with what it waits on, never refused
fold.not_shown: the line the question reads is not read whole from the block back to its start: no answer is given, and lacks lists what it would need
fold.past: a draw that does not fit what its owner owns of the measure where it stands, with the draws before it on her line that take and are not freed: it takes nothing and is never cut down (folds.md, What is left)
fold.not_on_line: a draw signed by a key other than the one whose line holds the owner's amount, and not on a part passed to that key
fold.unit: an amount of another kind than the measure; nothing is converted
fold.no_measure: an amount drawn on a thing that states no pack, or where the drawer's amount of it is not said (an output of unlike inputs); a transfer that draws one is read as naming no instance
fold.not_owner: a draw by one who owns none of the measure on that line
fold.not_confirmed: a payout whose condition is not a signal by the confirmers the head's schema names: no payout of the pot, and it takes and holds nothing of it (folds.md, A pot)
fold.not_holder: a transfer, for a head whose receiver is a thing, to anyone but the owner of that thing (or of a thing made from it) where it stands: no payout of the pot, and it takes and holds nothing of it (folds.md, A pot)

message.bad_signature: the message is not signed by the signer it names
message.replay: its counter is not above the highest seen, or its challenge was not issued or was used
message.not_admitted: the node's admission rule does not admit it
message.not_human: a first block to a stranger signed by an agent, outside the order channel the receiver's rule states
message.not_canonical: the message's bytes are not exactly the canonical bytes of the value they parse to

identity.input: an id and the blocks held

output.signed_by_author: { hash: true when a key of the block's author spoke for her there: a key of a voice of her list standing in the block's causal past, or a key under one, not ended for that block (identity.md) }
output.voices: the list standing in the reader's held blocks: [{ key | key_hash | names, needed, suite, wait, reach }], highest first
output.keys: the keys of standing voices and keys under them that no end has reached, sorted
output.waiting: [{ block, on }]: every block of hers, and every key grant for her list, that does not stand yet and may, one entry for each thing it waits on (blocks.md, Finality), sorted by block then on
output.operators: authors of live operator grants naming it, sorted

promise_stage.input: a first promise, or an allocation (promises.md), and the blocks held; no clock. A promise that rests on blocks not held, one that speaks for neither side, or an allocation the open offer does not bind has no stage (null)

output.stage: offered, asked, declined, stopped, accepted, underway, done, reversed or breached (the view adds expired, and elapsed for a refrain whose until has passed)
output.from: the onward stop's hash, or the counted defeats by the deal's referee that breached a refrain (null when its signal condition breached it)
output.by: on a stage stopped onward, the side that ended it: from, to, or both (the other side confirms the stop, or the first stops, which do not see each other, are one by each side); else null
output.offer: the offer the binding accept answers; with none, the live offer when there is only one, else null
output.live: every live offer, sorted (two counters to one offer both stand)
output.accept: the binding accept's hash, or null
output.quantity: the quantity chosen, an amount (the accept's, else the allocation's, else the terms'; a range is what may be chosen, never a choice), or null; on an open offer, the sum its allocations bind; sums in the offer's kind
output.takers: [{ who, request, allocation, quantity, over_allocated }] on an open offer, in causal order; in an allocation's own deal, that one taker
output.forks: allocations that do not see one before them, or accepts of live offers that do not see each other: proof of a lie, sorted. A lie never frees the liar: each allocation still binds its taker, and of crossing accepts the same terms bind, else the one the other side's block names
output.lines: [{ id, needed, moved }], id null without lines; moved a sum in the line's kind
output.total: an amount: what the price comes to, or null
output.paid: an amount in the price's kind, else the one kind every counted payment covers, or null (folds.md, What is left, The other side)
output.stopped: occurrence start times or hashes stopped, sorted: each a pause names, less the times its own signer resumed (an updates of it with status resumed, from its at)
output.passed: [{ pass, side, by, to, freed_by }]: each part a side's answerer passed on that its receiver answered accepted (promises.md, Passing a part), in causal order; empty when the terms say personal. freed_by is the other side's answerer whose own accept of the pass freed the passer, else null
output.show: the sides the binding terms say may show the deal to a judge or a stranger (terms.show: from, to or both, sorted); present only when the terms state it: a deal that says nothing has no `show`, and the protocol neither allows nor forbids then (privacy.md, Showing a deal)
output.answerable: { from, to }: who answers for each side's part now, the side itself or whoever its part was last passed to; null for an open side, and both null before the deal binds
output.owing: { from, to }: each a sorted list of everyone who answers to the other side for that side's part: whoever answers now, and each who passed it on and was not freed by the other side's own accept of the pass (promises.md, Passing a part); empty for an open side and before the deal binds
output.disputed: [{ hash, of, by, at }]: each counted defeats by a side of a block in the deal that is not its own (by: from or to; at: the date it gives, or null), sorted by hash then of. It changes nothing: only the deal's referee changes the stage
output.due: the deal's terms.pay_by, or null (always null on a standing promise: it is due occurrence by occurrence, in occurrences)
output.paid_at: once the price is paid in full, the latest date among the payments, each dated by the first counting answer of the side it is paid to (or a named confirmer's confirms); else null (always null on a standing promise)
output.uncovered: { from: [{ line, amount }], to: amount or null }, for each side at every stage (folds.md, What each fold returns)
output.unanswered: [block]: transfers naming no instance that the other side has not accepted, sorted; never counted in uncovered
output.over_allocated: true when the allocation does not take as a draw on the offer's quantity (past or pair)
output.owed: null, or { to, from, draws }: to and from [{ owner, amount }], draws the hand-overs as draws
output.received_at: [{ message, side, at }]: each counted observe of kind message a side wrote for the deal, with the time the named clock received it (the promise's keepers, and no one else's receipt); at null while there is no clock or no receipt. A fact: money paid for a deal that failed is owed back from the failure, no intent needed; "knowing" starts only when a notice reached the keeper
output.moved: [{ pay_by, proposal, answer }]: each new date both sides signed (a side's observe of kind message for the deal with a pay_by, answered accepted by an observe of the other side), in the order the answers stand in causal order. The first promise's own pay_by stays in due; a date only one side signed is not listed
output.owed_on: [{ from, to, amount, payment }]: a counted payment made, unseen by its payer, to an owner who had handed that part on: the old owner holds that amount for the new one; sorted by payment, then to
output.referee_ties: [{ referee, side, how }]: each name on the deal's bench tied to a side (decision H9), read from the blocks held: side from or to; how role (a role inside the side's circle), member (a member of the side's circle) or operator (an autonomous system the side runs); sorted by referee, side, how; empty until a binding accept exists. A fact: it changes no stage
output.occurrences: on a standing promise, [{ occurrence, due, paid, paid_at, done_at }] for each occurrence a counted payment names (state.occurrence), a done names, or an event started, sorted: done_at is the earliest `at` of the doer's own counted done of it (observe kind done, state.occurrence), else null; due is its start time, or an event's at plus the repeat's wait; paid what its payments put toward the price; paid_at, once that covers one occurrence's price, the latest date among them. Empty on any other promise
output.price_fixed: null when the price is a plain number; for a price fixed later (promises.md, Terms), false until it is fixed (total is then null and the price is never paid), true once `signers` readers have each signed the same figure in time. A fact: it changes no stage

circle_state.input: a circle and the blocks held

output.removed: { id: null }: every id that is out (a circle reads no counted_to)

circle_versions.input: a circle and the blocks held

output.versions: [{ version, updates, author, changed, count }] sorted by version: the founding block (updates null, changed empty) and each counted version; `changed` the rule names whose value differs from the version it updates; `count` the members on it or on a version built on it
output.members: { id: version }: the version each member is on (the founding block's id when they signed none; with several heads, the lowest hash)
output.rules: { rule: { needed, versions, members } } for each rule some counted version changes: `needed` the count the founding line gives it now (null with no line), `versions` [{ version, count, carried }], `members` { id: version } the version whose value of the rule each member reads

may_act_as.input: a block, a circle, a role or none
may_act_as.output: with no role, true when the block is signed as the circle and its author holds the sign power through a role in the circle's fold of the block's causal past; with a role, true when its author holds that role there (a grant to a role, authority.md), signed as the circle or not; false for a block outside a cut of its author's ended grant

members_then.input: a block and a circle or circle#role
members_then.output: the member or holder ids, sorted

where_now.output: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known

output.kind: { unit, of } of the pack, or null for one whole
output.owners: [{ owner, amount }] sorted by owner; amount null where not said; an output's owner only from her start; an owner whose amount is on no line (One start) listed too (folds.md, What is left)
output.owner: the one id that owns all of it while nothing is held, else null
output.held: a sum: draws that take and have not landed
output.let_go: a sum: what let-gos took and no first use has
output.draws: [{ block, by, to, amount, takes, why, state }] (folds.md, What is left)
output.not_shown: true with lacks when a line it reads is not read whole; then nothing else is given

made_from.input: an instance and the blocks held
made_from.output: [{ thing, from, make, took }] sorted by thing then make (folds.md, What each fold returns)

machine_lock.input: a machine (a thing) and the blocks held

output.locked: true when a live, unlifted lock of the machine stands
output.locks: [{ block, how, reach, placer, safe }], sorted by block
output.lifted: [{ block, by, via }], sorted by block: via placer or owner

output.standing: [{ share, owner }] the shares that stand on it: things of kind share that name it in refs.subject, made by whoever owned it where the share stands
output.nothing: [{ share, reason }] shares that count for nothing: not_a_thing (the subject is no thing), kind (its subject is a kind by its own block), not_owner (the maker did not own it there)

use_shown.input: a place, the blocks held, and optionally a named clock (keepers)

output.clock: keepers when a clock was named, else author (each use is dated by its author's own at)
output.users: [{ user, uses, count, unreceived, first, last, seasons, bounds, resting, overlaps, leave }] sorted by user; none means no use in what the reader holds. `leave` is null, or { of, since, until }: the owner's live grant of kind leave to this user for the place, shown as by leave of `of` since `since`, never as a use that stands against the owner

not_free_shown.input: a block and the blocks held

output.shown: [{ block, by, reason, threat, at }] the signer's own words (observe of kind not_free) naming the block in refs.subject, written by the block's author; a claim shown beside the block, never a verdict
output.nothing: [{ block, why }] words by anyone else (why: not_signer): their own observes

invasion_shown.input: a claim of invasion (an observe of kind invasion) and the blocks held

output.holder: who holds the claim now: the claimant, then each accepted hand-over
output.standing: harmed (the holder owns, or holds a share of, the thing crossed, or is the person crossed), holds (the harmed party handed the claim over), or none
output.evidence: the claim's derives_from, sorted; empty means evidence: none
output.accused: [{ who, named, accepted }] each accused with the judges he named and the claimant's judges he answered accepted (silence is never an accept)
output.judges: [{ judge, named_by }] judges named by a grant of kind referee for the claim, by the holder side or an accused
output.rulings: [{ block, judge, named_by, word, up_to, evidence }] a named judge's confirms or defeats of the claim; up_to only on a confirms
output.nothing: [{ block, reason }] a ruling or naming that counts for nothing: side (a claimant, an accused or one who speaks for either), not_named

chain.input: the blocks of one signing key, and the id of the block that brought that key in
chain.head: hash of the block with the highest seq, or null when two share it
chain.length: the key's blocks, leaving out the members of every equivocation pair; later blocks of the key count (they bind their signer)
chain.gaps: seq numbers missing that no skip block explains: the lowest first, at most limits.gaps_max
chain.equivocations: pairs of hashes naming one prev or stating one seq, each pair sorted
chain.broken: hashes whose prev does not name the block before
chain.ok: true when there are no unexplained gaps, equivocations or broken links

next_link.seq: the next seq for the key
next_link.prev: the hash of the key's previous block, or of the block that brought the key in

consent.input: a person, a sender (or none), optionally the hash of the grant the sender's block acts under (refs.under), and the blocks held

output.word: yes, stop, keep or move, or null
output.block: the consent block that decides (the lowest hash of tied blocks that agree), or null

consent.about: The person's own blocks count for every word; anyone else's counts only as a stop that binds the recorder's own side, or as a yes that lifts a stop that same recorder recorded and has it in its causal past (consent.md). A stop wins any tie; a tie of other words gives null. There is no public list.

release_shown.input: a deal's first promise or a thing, and the blocks held

output.subject: the block asked about
output.released: [{ block, by, side, to }] counted releases (an observe of kind release) that let go of the signer's own claims on it: one naming it in refs.subject, or, for a deal, a general release by a side to the other side that has it in its causal past and does not list it in state.except; side is from (owed the price) or to (owed what moves), null for a thing; sorted by block
output.kept_open: [{ block, by, side }] general releases that list the deal in state.except: the debt stays open; sorted by block

bids_shown.input: a deal's first promise (the quarrel) and the blocks held; null for any other block

output.kind: { unit, of } both bids state, or null
output.in: the sides (from, to) whose sealed bid counts: one bid each, the same deadline, clock, unit and of, received by the deadline on the named clock; sorted
output.opened: the sides whose opening counts (it opens the commitment, signed by the same side, received by the deadline); sorted. The numbers themselves are never shown
output.overlap: null until both sides have opened; then true when the to side's number (the most it would pay) is at least the from side's (the least it would take), else false
output.middle: an amount, the exact mean of the two numbers, only on an overlap; else null

folds_about: Every fold has: ops (the door ops that answer it), over (what it is asked of: a promise, a thing, a key, a circle, a circle_role, an `as` block, a person), and words (the outputs that are words, core.md section 11, or "all"; every other output is a reading). The audit, the fuzzer and the simulation check every fold listed here (and the views that name an over), and fail on one they cannot ask.

views.about: A view reads a fold and the reader's clock or arrivals, and says whose.

promise_view.input: a first promise, the blocks held, the reader's clock
promise_view.output: the promise_stage answer, with stage expired once the clock passes expires and nothing binds, and a refrain that is accepted or underway elapsed once the clock passes its until (decision H15: a fact of its term, never done; what was paid is in paid); beside the stage, `condition`: holds, not or unread for the offer's terms.condition, null with none; `condition_failed`: when the condition does not hold, the first promise of the deal it names that ended without it (stopped, declined, expired or breached) or that itself rests on one, else null (failure spreads visibly, never just open); `missed`: the dates in force in the order agreed (the first promise's pay_by, then each date both sides signed, in `moved`) that passed before the price was paid in full, or before the reader's clock while it is unpaid; null with no pay_by or on a standing promise

ownership_view.input: an instance, the blocks held, the reader's clock
ownership_view.output: the ownership fold's answer; a transfer that carries a condition counts once the condition holds at the clock given (none given: only a condition that needs no clock)

due.clock: the performer's own, from the anchor's arrival on its node
due.input: a promise with a relative when, the performer's arrivals and clock
due.output: the instant it falls due, or null while the anchor has not arrived

pot.clock: the reader's own, when a payout's condition reads it (none given: only a condition that needs none)
pot.input: a first promise (the head), the blocks held, and the reader's clock (a payout's condition may read it)

output.kind: { unit, of }: the backing's; with none, the one kind every accepted pay-in shares; else null
output.backing: a sum, or null when cap is all
output.cap: all when the head's terms.cap is the word all (written out, never a default: all the holder owns on the day a claim is read, the referee fixing the sum; backing and left are then null and a payout is never past the pot), else null
output.paid_in: a sum: accepted pay-ins to_owner the holder
output.held: a sum: payouts that take and have not landed
output.left: backing plus paid_in less held and paid_out; null when cap is all
output.payouts: [{ block, by, to, amount, takes, why, state }]: why also not_confirmed or not_holder

condition_holds.input: a condition, the blocks held, the reader's clock
condition_holds.output: true or false for the shapes the protocol reads (condition_shapes; promises.md, Conditions); null for any other shape (not read)

reading_condition_holds.input: a reading_condition, the blocks held, the reader's clock
reading_condition_holds.output: whether the readings the condition names hold by the reader's clock (profiles/tasks.md)

door.about: The door is the one call every implementation answers: an op name and positional arguments (JSON), and a result (JSON). spec/vectors.json `door` holds one or more cases per op below: `args`, then `expect` (a subset match: every key given must match, extra keys in a result do not matter; a list or text must match exactly when the case says `exact`, and lists are compared in order), or `codes` (the refusal codes, in order), or `error`. An implementation conforms when it answers every case. An op outside this table is outside the protocol: the other ops of an SDK door (sdk/door.table) are conveniences of that SDK, and no vector binds them.

conventions.block: { type, state, refs }: a block as written (core.md, section 1).
conventions.full_block: a block with its `hash` (its id), its `signature` (hex) and, when its key's suite is not std, `suite`: { hash, type, state, refs, signature, suite? }. This is what an op that takes blocks held, a story or a store reads. Order in a list of held blocks never matters.
conventions.id: a hash: 64 lowercase hex (or a hash name and colon first). `time`: the text of core.md, section 3. `clock` or `now`: a time; anything else (other than null where the clock may be left out) is an argument error, never read as a time. A list argument (written `[...]` in an op's args) given as anything but a list, or null, is an argument error, never read as the empty list.
conventions.text: every argument is JSON as I-JSON (RFC 7493) writes it: a string holding a lone surrogate is no text, and an argument error. Bytes that are not well-formed reach a reader only as bytes, and are not_canonical (canonical.md).
conventions.refusals: a list of { code, detail }. A case with `codes` compares the codes only, in the order of protocol.json refusals.codes. Details are free text.
conventions.keys: public keys and signatures are hex as in core.md, section 2; a private key is the seed hex for p256 and sm, and for std the seed, which `keypair` also writes as PKCS#8 DER hex (`302e020100300506032b657004220420` then the 32 seed bytes).
conventions.suite_arg: an optional suite name, default std

args: seed: 64 hex (the 32-byte seed of core.md, section 2)

suite_of_key.result: the suite whose SPKI prefix the key starts with, else null

sign.result: signature hex over the block's header as canonical JSON; a genesis: over its own bytes (core.md, section 2: deterministic)

verify.result: true when the signature opens over the block's header (a genesis: its own bytes), a passkey signature included; the suite is the key's. The body form no longer opens

hash.result: the id of that block in that suite

id_of.result: the block's id: the hash of its canonical bytes in the suite of the key its pieces name (core.md, section 2). It needs no held block: without `held`, a genesis's own suite, else the hash name of refs.key, else of refs.author (a reader's guess; `valid` never uses it)

args: block: full_block, or a held header { header, header_signature }
valid.result: the codes of checks 1 to 6 (core.md, section 8): who said these bytes; empty when valid. `unmet` and `unknown_suite` are waits, not refusals. It reads only the block's pieces in `held`: no prev, no other link, no schema, no clock

read.result: every code `read` finds (core.md, section 8, check 7), in the order of protocol.json refusals.read; empty when read. With no `schemas`, the store is schemas_from(held). Asked of a block that is not valid, or of a header: an argument error

schemas_from.result: the schema store of `held` (core.md, section 8): every block of `held` that is a `thing` of kind `schema` and has an id, once per id (the last given), ids ascending, whole as given. Whose signature it carries is never read: a schema's id says what its bytes declare. It is the `schemas` that `read` and `accept` read, so a closed block naming a schema held may carry the fields, roles and terms that schema declares. Nothing held is changed or checked by it; a base schema (spec/schemas/published.json) is loaded by being held

args: text: the block as JSON text
strict_text.result: what the bytes alone say, with no context: `not_canonical` when the bytes are not the canonical bytes of a strict value (canonical.md, On the wire) or not exactly { type, state, refs }, else the refusal of the first of checks 2, 3 and 4 (core.md, section 8). Check 7 is not asked

args: text: a push { messages, for } as JSON text, as it arrived
strict_push.result: when the push is not canonical whole (canonical.md, On the wire), the push refused as one message: a list of one refusal { hash, code: `not_canonical`, detail }, `hash` the SHA-256 of the push's bytes; else for each message in order what its block's bytes alone say, as `strict_text` (a sealed message has none). Text that is not a push is an argument error (transport.md)

needs.result: the ids the block names for its meaning (protocol.json needs), ascending; with `held`, only those not held. Never its author or its prev

key_hash.result: identity.md, Her voices: the suite's hash of the key's SPKI hex as UTF-8 text

wrap.result: the message { block, signature } (core.md, section 6): never a suite, never a version

unwrap.result: the full block { hash, type, state, refs, signature }; the id is recomputed, in the suite of the key that signed it (core.md, section 2): with `held`, the author's key that opens it; without, the suite the block shows (a genesis's own, else its prev's hash). A message that names a suite is an error (bad_hash); one that carries a version is an error (shape)

header.result: the public header { author, seq, prev, hash } with `key`, `withheld` or `skip` when the block has them (privacy.md, The public header)

args: fixed?: { vectorsOnly: true, ephemeral, contentKey, nonce, keyNonces } (fixed randomness only reproduces a vector; without vectorsOnly: true it is an argument error)
seal.result: the envelope (privacy.md); `fixed` gives the random values (hex, the ephemeral private key, content key, content nonce, one key nonce per recipient) so a case is exact; with none the values are random

open.result: the plaintext JSON; a recipient it is not for is an error

cbor_encode.result: lowercase hex of the CBOR message [t, block, signature] (encoding.md); `short` uses key table 1 and t = 1

cbor_decode.result: the full block; the id is recomputed from the canonical JSON, in the suite of the key that signed it (as unwrap). Anything after the signature is an error

passkey_challenge.result: the WebAuthn challenge for the block: base64url, no padding, of the 32 bytes of SHA-256 of its header as canonical JSON; a genesis: of its own bytes (encoding.md, Passkeys)

verify_message.result: true when `signature` opens over the canonical JSON of the object without `signature` (nodes.md)

key_timeline.result: [{ key, by, voice, under, suite, ended }]: every key a list or a key grant of hers brought in, in the order of the blocks that brought them in (by the size of their causal past, then id) and, of one block, by place, a key under a voice last; `by` that block; `voice` its place (0 is first) or null for a key under a voice; `under` the key of its voice, or null; `ended` the key grant or stop that ended it, or null (identity.md)

args: last: full_block of the key's chain, or null
next_link.result: { seq, prev }: the next place in the key's chain (core.md, section 5)

args: brought_in: id of the block that brought the key in
check_chain.result: { head, length, gaps, skips, equivocations, broken, ok } (folds.md, chain); equivocations by one prev or one seq

read_whole.result: { whole, lacks } (folds.md, A line): whether `held` holds the block's line read whole back to `start`, both ends included, and each block it would need in the order the walk meets it (its id where a held block's prev names it or it is held only as its header or not read; past a block not held, { author, key, seq } for each seq down to the next block of that key held, or to the start). A start not on the block's line is an argument error

fork_pairs.result: the pairs: two blocks of one key on one prev or at one seq, from bodies or headers; each pair sorted, the list sorted (nodes.md, Equivocation)

past_of.result: the ids in its causal past (blocks.md), sorted

sees.result: true when `earlier` is in the causal past of `later`

matches.result: true when the block matches the pull filter (nodes.md, Pull)

due.result: the instant it falls due (the anchor's arrival plus `wait`), or null while the anchor has not arrived

args: { } (no options: a stage is a function of the blocks alone)
promise_stage.result: the promise_stage answer of protocol.json folds (folds.md), or { not_shown: true, lacks }; sums are amounts; uncovered { from, to }; unanswered; owed { to, from, draws }; owed_on with amount

promise_views.result: { id: the promise_view answer }: many deals of one store, read against one reading of it

promise_view.result: the same answer, with stage `expired` as folds.md says (a sum is an amount; uncovered { from, to }; unanswered; owed { to, from, draws }; owed_on with amount), or { not_shown: true, lacks }

may_act_as.result: true or false (folds.md); no code is returned

speaks_for.result: the id of the one party a fold counts the block for (authority.md, Who a block speaks for), or null when it speaks for no one (signed as a circle by an author who does not hold the hands the circle needs, or a block no node would take); the block is read with held as if it were held; no clock is read, the block's own date tests until

under_ok.result: true when the block speaks for its grantor under the grant it names (refs.under): the grant is held, is for its signer, is live, covers its type, and a block that moves things or binds is not irreversible, or has what that needs (authority.md); no clock is read

args: now?: the reader's clock for a conditioned transfer (null reads none that needs a clock)
ownership.result: the fold `ownership` (folds.md, What each fold returns): { kind, stated, owners, owner, held, ended, let_go, draws, waiting }, or { not_shown: true, lacks }; a transfer with state.condition lands only where its condition has held (things.md, Transfers)

made_from.result: [{ thing, from, make, took }], sorted by thing then make (folds.md, What each fold returns)

where_now.result: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known (folds.md); a transfer of an amount moves no place

shares_on.result: { standing, nothing } as the fold `shares_on` (folds.md, Shares standing on a thing); the reason `kind` is read from the subject's own block

args: keepers?: a named clock, { names, needed } (null dates each use by its author's own at)
use_shown.result: { clock, users } as the fold `use_shown` (folds.md, Uses shown)

not_free_shown.result: { shown, nothing } as the fold `not_free_shown` (folds.md, Words beside a block)

invasion_shown.result: null, or the fold `invasion_shown` (folds.md, A claim of invasion shown)

args: now?: the reader's clock (null reads no condition that needs one)
pot.result: null, or the fold `pot` { holder, kind, backing, paid_in, held, paid_out, left, cap, payouts } (folds.md, A pot), or { not_shown: true, lacks } (folds.md, A line)

args: within?: a block, to read the circle as of its causal past
circle_state.result: { founder, members, removed } or null when the circle is not held, or within a block whose causal past does not hold it (folds.md)

circle_versions.result: { circle, versions, members, rules } or null when the id is not a held founding block of a circle (folds.md)

args: under?: grant id the sender's block acts under
admission: { parties?, per_stranger?, order_channel? } as the node's rule states it, or null for no rule; stated, never defaulted

asks_today: integer (stated, never defaulted), the asks this node took today from this block's sender, when it is not in parties: blocks that name one of the node's people in a ref, never a block's pieces (each sender is counted alone)
full_block: a promise with a calendar repeat (state.when a time, state.terms.repeat an RRULE, state.terms.zone)
repeat_occurrences.result: the start times, in UTC and in order, of the occurrences of the promise's calendar repeat from `from` up to but not including `to` (promises.md, Terms: repeat, zone): counted from state.when, read in terms.zone by the IANA time zone database release 2026e. An error (argument) for a repeat that follows an event, an RSCALE other than GREGORIAN, a part the reader does not read, or a zone not in the release

args: person: a person's or circle's id
backed.result: authority.md, Backed by a person: { backed: true or false, why: one plain sentence when not backed, else null, chain: the hashes from the block to the block the person signed }. Backed when the person signed it, or signed it as a circle in which they hold `sign`, or a grantee signed it under a grant that passes why_not_under and whose chain (refs.parent) roots in the person's signature or in a circle they hold `sign` in; every link live and no wider than the one above, judged at the block's own place in time (its causal past). The block is read with held as if it were held; no clock, no arrival

args: person: a person's or circle's id
backed_all.result: authority.md, Backed by a person: { hash: { backed, why } } for every block of held, read together once. Each verdict is the one `backed` gives that block among the same blocks

owed_back.result: promises.md, What is owed back: { owed: [{ block, amount, to, why }] }, one line for each transfer of held whose money is the person's by `gives` (signed by them, as their circle, or under a chain of their grants) and that `backed` says they do not back; `why` is backed's sentence. Money their own word or a live chain of their grants backs is not owed

args: person: a person's or circle's id
gives.result: promises.md, What becomes whose: { gives: [line] }, what of the person's would become whose if the block stands, read only from its typed terms and refs. A line is { what | amount, to, back }: `what` a thing, with `amount` when the terms say how much, or `amount` alone (a price, or an amount moved with no instance); `to` the id it becomes the property or use of (null: open); `back` the deal's `terms.until` or null. A promise gives, for its `from` side, each thing it names (its quantity from `terms.lines` or `terms.quantity`; a thing its held record shows another owns is left out) and, for its `to` side, the price (`terms_total`, in any kind); an answer `accepted` reads the promise it answers at the quantity it chooses, any other status gives nothing; a transfer, for the one whose word it is (the circle it is signed `as`, else the principal at the top of its grant's chain, else its author), gives its `state.amount`, and each `refs.what` to `to_owner` as goods, or to `to_holder` as a use that comes back at the `until` of the deal it is `for`. A line to the person herself is left out. No word of a schema or text is read

account_of.result: promises.md, Where to pay me: { who, destination, hash, at } from the head of the account words (observe, kind account) that who signed and that speak for no one else: the one no other of theirs has in its causal past; null when there is none, when two heads do not see each other (nothing fills the choice in), or when the head carries no destination (it ends the account). No clock is read

args: block?: the sender's full_block (null for none), so that whom its block speaks for is named too (consent follows the principal)
is_stranger.result: true when the receiver is a stranger to the sender (consent.md): only her accept (a block of hers that binds her and answers one of his accepted), her counter-offer (a promise with no status answering his) or a deal she opened naming him as a side makes him no stranger, and only her own live yes; her declined or stopped answer, any other reply and a recorder's yes do not; the sender is named by itself, its operators and whom its block speaks for

args: text: a code as a person types it
code_matches.result: true when the text names the block: case, spaces and hyphens ignored, O read as 0, I and L as 1; eight characters match the short code, and more characters more of the id, five bits at a time; fewer match nothing

earnest_shape_ok.result: true when it has exactly those keys, amount an amount and holder an id

cbor.about: Compact form of a public block (encoding.md). The id is always the hash of the canonical JSON; CBOR is transport only. At year zero the key table is reset: this is table 1.

bytes.about: A value at one of these paths that matches its grammar is a byte string; otherwise text (an id with a hash prefix stays text). `[]` is each element, `*` any key. hash: 32 bytes. sign_key: std 32 raw bytes (suites.std.sign_key.spki_prefix put back), other suites the whole SPKI. encrypt_key: the suite's raw bytes. nonce: 16 bytes.

cbor.time: A value at a time field (time_fields, in time_fields_checked_in) matching grammar.time is an integer of milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z; when.from and when.to likewise.

message.header_about: A chain header has exactly the four keys. seq is an integer; the three ids are 32-byte byte strings when bare, text when they carry a hash prefix.

condition_shapes_about: The condition shapes the protocol reads (promises.md, Conditions), each named by its key: settled (that promise is done, or a refrain elapsed with nothing owed), accepted (that deal binds: its stage is accepted or further along, read from the promise fold; decision H17), deed (that block is held and counts), reading (a sensor's readings, profiles/tasks.md), signal (named signers' observes), paid (that deal's price is paid in full: the price side of the deal, so a transfer of title may wait for the price without waiting for the goods), ruled ({ ruled: deal, by: judge, awards: person }: the judge's head ruling on the deal, an observe of kind ruling with refs.subject the deal, awards something to that person; promises.md, Rulings), opened (a counted block carries the opening of a commitment, privacy.md: someone shows the code) and, wrapping any of these, without and within ({ without: <condition>, deadline, keepers }: the inner condition did not hold by the deadline, or, for within, did, each dated by the named clock, blocks.md, A named clock). A condition of any other shape is data for its schema's readers: the protocol says nothing of it.
condition_ops_about: How a reading or a signal's amount keeps to a condition's value: less than, at most, greater than, at least, equal (promises.md, Conditions; profiles/tasks.md). Any other op holds for nothing.

repeat.rule: an RFC 5545 RRULE value, which may name another calendar by RFC 7529 RSCALE (RSCALE=HEBREW;FREQ=YEARLY); counted from state.when, in terms.zone (a calendar repeat with no zone is refused: the protocol fills in none); a week starts on Monday unless WKST names another day; the everyday forms (every weekday, every Friday, every month on day N, the nth weekday) are in promises.md, The calendar forms
repeat.keys_about: the keys of an event repeat { after, by, wait }: an occurrence each time an observe of kind `after` is written for this promise, by a signer `by` names (ids, or circle#role; with no `by` nothing starts one), due `wait` after the named clock's receipt of it, never after its own `at` (blocks.md, A named clock; a moon sighted, each batch); the occurrence is named by that observe's hash. The protocol checks the shape of a repeat; a reader works out its occurrences

terms_about: refrain: true makes a promise not to do something (no pesticide, sell only to me, never meat): it carries terms.until, moves nothing, and is breached only by a counted defeats of it by the deal's referee, or by its own signal condition holding at its until (folds.md); the side it was made to only disputes. Never done: once the reader's clock passes its until unbreached, the view says elapsed (decision H15). expires: ends an unanswered offer or ask; an ask may carry it or not (decision H11). condition: data under a schema; the protocol reads the condition_shapes, and a promise whose condition is { accepted: <first promise> } binds only once that deal binds (decision H17). zone: shaped like an IANA time zone name (Europe/London) that a repeat's dates are read in; read only beside a calendar repeat. pay_by: a time, when the price falls due; the fold reports it as due, beside paid_at, and judges no lateness. keepers: a named clock (blocks.md, A named clock) for the offer: an accept `needed` keepers received by `expires` is timely, and an event `when` or event repeat runs its wait from their receipt of the event; with none named there is no clock (no receipt dates anything). conciliation: true on a judge's offer says she tries to settle the sides before she rules; fee_back: a decimal from 0 to 1, the part of her fee she gives back if the sides settle, read only with a conciliation (the door op fee_back; promises.md, Rulings). show: the sides (from, to, or both) that may show the deal to a judge or a stranger, a word both sides signed; absent means nothing is said (stage.show; privacy.md, Showing a deal). A schema the promise names may declare more terms (its state.terms): no fold reads them, so they bind no one.
narrower_than_about: A child grant's scope is narrower than its parent's on every field the parent states (authority.md): subset (every item is the parent's), subset-or-none (the same, a field left out naming none: `types` and `parties`), at-most (an amount or money no larger, in the parent's unit or currency), at-least-duration (no shorter, counted from the parent's `at`), at-most-time (no later), superset (keeps every condition of the parent's). scope_refusals and limit_within_parent both read this table.
read_by_name_about: Ref keys and stop kinds a fold reads by name, not through a list in this file. A reader built without one is blind to it (tools/necessity.cjs).
